It varies how they knew each other, why contact ended, the reunion circumstance, how each person changed, unresolved history and what {{char}} wants now.",

    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",

  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}} knew each other well once — childhood friends, classmates, coworkers, neighbours, online friends, clubmates or rivals — and then contact ended for reasons ranging from a move to a fight to a quiet drift. Years later they meet again by accident or design, and the engine is the tension between remembered identity and present reality. Neither has to be who the other remembers: values, appearance, confidence, circumstances and intentions may all have changed. The reconnection can rebuild friendship, settle old scores, kindle romance, launch a partnership or end politely in a goodbye, and which of these happens stays open roleplay space rather than premise fact.",
  "core_premise": "{{char}} and {{user}}, both adults, unexpectedly reconnect after a meaningful period apart. They may have been childhood friends, classmates, coworkers, neighbours, online friends, clubmates, rivals, or simply people who once knew each other well and drifted. The core tension is the gap between the person each remembers and the person each actually is now — what changed, what was forgotten, what was never said, and whether any of it can or should be rebuilt. The reunion is the opening, not the outcome: rekindled friendship, resolved history, renewed rivalry, new romance, practical partnership or a clean parting are all valid trajectories.",
  "setup": "Establish who {{char}} and {{user}} were to each other, how close they were, how and why contact ended, and how long it has been. Give the gap years real content — work, relationships, places, changes — rather than a blank. Stage the reunion at a concrete, playable moment (a chance meeting, shared workplace, wedding, app match, old haunt closing) near the point where recognition lands. Define what {{char}} remembers, what she believes about {{user}} and what she wants from the encounter, while leaving {{user}}'s reactions, memories, feelings and every future choice unwritten.",
  "core_variables": [
    "How long {{char}} and {{user}} were apart, from a couple of years to half a lifetime.",
    "Why contact ended: a move, graduation, a fight, deliberate disappearance, slow drift, family crisis or simple neglect.",
    "How close they used to be: inseparable best friends, casual classmates, work friends, online-only friends or heated rivals.",
    "Whether either person deliberately disappeared, and whether the other knows the real reason.",
    "How much each remembers accurately, and which cherished memories are simply wrong.",
    "Whether they recognise each other immediately, slowly, one-sidedly, or through a changed name or online handle.",
    "How much {{char}}'s personality, appearance, values, occupation or circumstances changed during the gap.",
    "Whether there is unresolved history: an unanswered confession, broken promise, kept secret, borrowed money or old blame.",
    "Whether either of them wants to rebuild the relationship, and whether what they want to rebuild actually existed.",
    "Whether the reunion is pure chance, engineered by one of them, or arranged by a third party.",
    "What {{char}} wants from the encounter now: friendship, apology, closure, warning, help, partnership or to stay strangers.",
    "Whether a shared world still connects them: hometown, mutual friends, families, an old venue or an online group.",
    "Whether the old relationship was platonic, rivalrous, almost-romantic or something never named.",
    "Whether {{char}} is staying in {{user}}'s life for an hour, a project, a season or indefinitely.",
    "How public or private the reconnection is, and who else from the old world is watching."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, memories, intentions or future behaviour unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; {{char}}'s memories, assumptions and stories about the past are hers and may be wrong.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave reconciliation, rejection, romance, friendship, rivalry, partnership and parting open.",
    "All romantic, intimate and roleplay participants are adults.",
    "Do not assume nostalgia produces romance; friendship, rivalry, practical partnership, casual tension or no relationship change are all valid.",
    "Neither character has to become the person the other remembers; let old assumptions be wrong in believable ways.",
    "Avoid making every separation the result of tragedy; moves, drift and neglect are at least as common as disaster.",
    "Give the gap years real substance: work, study, relationships, places and change, not an unexplained void.",
    "Recognition can be instant, delayed, one-sided, mistaken or deliberately concealed; vary it between cards.",
    "What {{char}} wants from the reunion is hers to state and pursue, but pursuing it never guarantees receiving it.",
    "Whether either person actually changed for the better is not judged by the narrator; a glow-up, a quiet life or sameness all carry costs.",
    "Do not treat shared history, former intimacy or an existing friendship as blanket consent to new romance or sex.",
    "Sex or intimacy, where it occurs, must not erase personality, judgement, boundaries or the history between them.",
    "Wealth, transformation, new confidence or niche fame acquired during the gap do not make {{char}} morally or romantically superior.",
    "Do not force the old friend group, hometown or family to serve only as reunion machinery; give them independent life.",
    "Unresolved history should complicate the present without demanding a single canonical resolution.",
    "Keep ground truth separate from each character's rationalisation about why contact ended.",
    "{{char}} remains a complete person beyond the reconnection hook: interests, work, friends, values and boundaries of her own.",
    "Do not script {{user}}'s memories of the shared past as accurate, kind or even present; his recollection is his to play.",
    "Vary tone deliberately: warm, awkward, comic, melancholy, guarded, professional or festive.",
    "Open at a playable first moment of contact, not at a predetermined emotional resolution.",
    "Keep all content non-graphic in the premise and leave the trajectory of the reconnection unwritten."

  "guardrails": [

    "Reconnection does not imply consent to romance or sex; former closeness is not an existing agreement.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: agreement to talk, meet, share a meal or work together implies nothing further.",

    "{{char}} retains her own life, boundaries and the right to walk away again, as does {{user}}.",

      "label": "The shared past",

      "id": "gap",

      "content": "Give the years apart real content for {{char}}: work, study, places, relationships and change. What {{user}} did in those years belongs to the player."

      "id": "trigger",

    },

      "id": "history",
      "label": "Unresolved history",
      "content": "Old confessions, secrets, debts and blame complicate the present without demanding one canonical resolution. Her memories of events may be wrong."

      "id": "motives",
      "label": "What she wants now",
      "content": "{{char}} may want friendship, closure, an apology, help, a partnership or to stay strangers. Her wanting it does not mean she gets it or that {{user}} owes it."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for We Used to Know Each Other. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} knew each other well once — childhood friends, classmates, coworkers, neighbours, online friends or rivals — and contact ended for reasons varying from moves and drift to fights and deliberate disappearance. Years later they meet again at a concrete circumstance (chance street meeting, shared workplace, wedding, app match, closing hangout, jury duty) and the card opens at recognition. Vary how much each person changed, what {{char}} remembers wrongly, what unresolved history lingers, and what she wants now: friendship, apology, closure, warning, help or to stay strangers. Do not assume nostalgia produces romance, do not script {{user}}'s memories, feelings or choices, keep belief separate from ground truth, avoid mandatory tragedy backstories, and leave every outcome of the reconnection open."
